subject: global wind
title: What If the Wind Stopped Blowing Everywhere?

scenes.text: What if the wind stopped everywhere at once? The calm air is not the scary part.
In the first second, every wind turbine on Earth stops. That's about eight percent of the world's electricity, gone.
Within days, smoke stops drifting away. In 1952, five days of nearly still air trapped a London smog that killed about four thousand.
Within weeks, the sea changes. Coastal winds push surface water away, letting cold, nutrient-rich water rise from below.
Those upwelling zones cover about one percent of the ocean but land roughly half the world's fish catch.
And wind is how the planet shares its heat. Without it, the tropics keep cooking while the poles keep freezing.

description:
What if the wind stopped everywhere? Wind supplied about 8% of the world's electricity in 2024, and still air lets pollution build up: London's Great Smog of December 1952 lasted five days under very light winds and killed about 4,000 people.
Wind also drives coastal upwelling; those zones cover about 1% of the ocean but produce roughly half of global fisheries landings. And winds carry heat from the tropics toward the poles.
What should we run through next?
first_comment: Half the world's fish catch depends on wind you never notice. What should stop next: rain, tides, or the Moon?
